request.questionText: Recall that "statistical uncertainty" is concerned with repeatability. Your results are "certain" if the results are repeatable (i.e., you observe little fluctuation in summary estimates) across different samples from the same random data-generating process.Which of the following is among the reasons that bootstrapping works as a practical tool for statistical inference? Select all accurate statements.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Resampling creates synthetic variability for our statistical summaries (i.e., sample estimates), helping us to quantify our uncertainty related to sampling variance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bootstrapping uses Monte Carlo simulation to approximate the variability that we would observe IF it were feasible to sample repeatedly from the same population.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In the context of statistical inference, uncertainty arises from randomness inherent to our sampling procedure, not as a characteristic of any one particular sample generated by that procedure.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Summary statistics (i.e., sample estimates) from different bootstrap samples will differ from one another—and theamountby which they differ from one another provides us a quantitative measure of our statistical uncertainty.
